summary: DeepSeek V4 config loading now accepts the Transformers >=4.57 compress_rates and rope_parameters names, preserves the legacy aliases used by SGLang, rejects conflicting duplicate aliases, and remains compatible with legacy config.json files. The pinned Transformers 5.12.1 stack previously rejected compress_rates during AutoConfig construction before reaching the originally reported missing-attribute crash; the post-change end-to-end ModelConfig reproduction succeeds.

tests.what_was_measured: 12 unit tests passed, including new-schema, legacy-schema, equal dual-alias, conflicting-alias, custom/remote-config fallback, indexer-count, and existing model-config regression coverage.

tests.command: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-9d51d02baf78/venv/bin/python - <<'PY' # construct ModelConfig from the retained local Transformers >=4.57-style config fixture
tests.what_was_measured: The actual ModelConfig path loaded compress_rates=[0,4,128,0], exposed compress_ratios, normalized rope_parameters/rope_scaling, and initialized attention scaling. The same command failed before the change with StrictDataclassFieldValidationError for compress_rates.
Repository formatting, lint, spelling, syntax, secret, and registered-test metadata checks passed for every changed Python file.

gpu_evidence: The assigned AMD Instinct MI350X was visible through torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2, but this change is limited to CPU-side JSON/config parsing and performs no tensor or kernel computation. A GPU numerical run would not exercise the changed code.
remaining_limitations: No DeepSeek V4 model weights were provided, so full engine startup, weight loading, and serving were not executed. The retained ModelConfig reproduction exercises the reported config-loading failure but does not qualify DeepSeek V4 semantic accuracy or distributed execution.

The pinned environment contains Transformers 5.12.1, not exactly 4.57.x. Both are on the new-name side of the reported schema transition; exact 4.57.x execution was not performed because the pinned software stack was preserved.
No native library was changed or rebuilt; native compilation is not applicable to this Python-only configuration compatibility fix.
